independent_field_counting_rule: Does not add support to any of the four specific sparse technique classes until case-level technique labels and identities are inspected.

field_or_case: Zama oil field (X2X and Z3Z pools)
source_summary: Published field case describes acid-gas injection at Zama with CO2 and H2S and monitoring relevant to EOR. A separate technical history reports acid gas injection concurrent with oil production in X2X and a later miscible flood in Z3Z; count the named field once, not pools separately.
attributes_reported: carbonate reservoir; acid gas CO2/H2S evidence; pool-specific injection history
independent_field_counting_rule: At most one independent field group for Zama regardless of how many pools or papers are found.
blocking_gaps: Extract the primary paper and corroborating primary field history; verify that the specific interval meets the repository's Miscible acid gas target semantics; retrieve full feature provenance; avoid treating sequestration alone as EOR.

source_summary: Journal article describes a field application context using natural energy and hot-water flooding and a pilot area; its intervention context must be distinguished from the viscosity-reducer pilot reported in that paper.
attributes_reported: reported depth range; porosity; permeability; oil viscosity
independent_field_counting_rule: At most one field group for J8 block.
blocking_gaps: API gravity, pressure, initial/current oil saturation and compatible feature ranges are not all established in the readily visible abstract; confirm the label against the full source.

independent_field_counting_rule: At most one independent field group for Yates.

source_summary: The SPE PetroWiki synthesis is specifically about nitrogen miscible floods and names Jay Field. The cited N2-WAG history therefore cannot be counted as a Nitrogen immiscible case without separate primary evidence for a different immiscible project.

independent_field_counting_rule: At most one field group for Jay/Jay LEC; count only a separately identified immiscible project if primary evidence documents one.

source_summary: DOE report documents a named nitrogen-flood project, but its title identifies a miscible nitrogen flood, so it is not evidence for the Nitrogen immiscible class.

independent_field_counting_rule: Do not count toward Nitrogen immiscible; keep as a potential unrelated-class evaluation lead only.

field_or_case: Unnamed North Viking Graben Tarbert horizon
source_summary: EU project summary describes a completed analysis of an existing immiscible gas scheme and estimates incremental recovery, but the proposed nitrogen pilot was not pursued and the field is not identified by a canonical name in the public summary.
attributes_reported: immiscible gas scheme; Tarbert formation; study outcome
independent_field_counting_rule: Do not count until a source-resolved field identity and actual implemented technique are established.
blocking_gaps: Pilot not pursued; named field identity unresolved; method class and original operational context require primary source review.

source_summary: A 2020 worldwide field-application review lists Liaohe Tuo 33 in its N2-injection table as immiscible; reported porosity 2.4–9.8%, permeability 7–28.4 mD, depth 1200–1530 m, temperature 58 C and oil viscosity about 49.95 mPa s. Same named field is also described as an N2-foam pilot elsewhere in the review.
attributes_reported: porosity; permeability; depth; temperature; viscosity; formation; project interval
independent_field_counting_rule: At most one field group for Liaohe Tuo 33 across the conventional N2 and N2-foam project descriptions.
blocking_gaps: Primary Zhu (2016) source not yet extracted; API, oil saturation and source-compatible pressure/context not present in reviewed table; exact canonical field identity and overlap with OGJ2014/v1 manifest not audited.

source_summary: A worldwide EOR field review describes a named N2-foam field test with porosity, permeability, depth, temperature and viscosity ranges. Foam injection is not automatically equivalent to the repository's Nitrogen immiscible target.

independent_field_counting_rule: One canonical field group only; count only after the source-defined technique maps to the target taxonomy.
blocking_gaps: Primary source and target semantics need review; API and oil saturation are absent from the accessible table; overlap not checked.

technique_class_candidate: HC immiscible candidate with cross-source technique conflict
source_summary: One review characterises a historical lean-hydrocarbon-gas injection episode as immiscible, while another EOR field table describes miscible nitrogen injection at Ekofisk. These may be separate injection episodes; the field name alone cannot identify the technique-specific record.
attributes_reported: fractured chalk; separate lean-HC and miscible-N2 histories reported
independent_field_counting_rule: Ekofisk is one canonical field group across its different projects; never use it as an unseen field if any Ekofisk episode occurs in training.
blocking_gaps: Primary project dates/injectant identity/target semantics and exact training-manifest overlap must be resolved; full compatible v2 core vector not verified.

source_summary: A review cites a pilot of immiscible hydrocarbon-gas foam at Woodbine Field and reports harsh reservoir conditions including about 120 C and 3.23% salinity. The evidence is for foam injection, not automatically the plain HC immiscible flood class.
attributes_reported: temperature; salinity; field name; injection process
independent_field_counting_rule: At most one field group for Woodbine Field.
blocking_gaps: Need the cited primary pilot paper, measured v1/v2 input features and confirmation that foam is in scope for the nine-class target; overlap not audited.

independent_field_counting_rule: One field group for Cantarell-Akal; don't count individual reservoirs or wells separately.

independent_field_counting_rule: At most one field group for Slaughter Estate Unit.

source_summary: The IEAGHG report describes a 1995 acid-gas injection operation with approximately 20% H2S/80% CO2, carbonate-reef properties around 6% porosity, 150 mD permeability, 65 C and 15.5 MPa. attributes_reported: carbonate reef; porosity; permeability; temperature; pressure; nearby oil API context
independent_field_counting_rule: Do not count as an EOR class example unless source evidence explicitly confirms implemented EOR recovery rather than disposal.
blocking_gaps: Technique target not established; no complete source-compatible feature record or v1 overlap audit.

source_summary: A 2023 field-technology review refers to Jha et al. (2018) describing a hot-water flooding field test in multi-layered onshore oil fields in South Lokichar Basin; the design injection temperature is reported as 90 C. This is stronger than a laboratory lead but the primary field-test paper and its exact reservoir identity/data must still be reviewed.
attributes_reported: hot-water test; designed injection temperature 90 C; basin identity
independent_field_counting_rule: One independently confirmed field group only after the canonical oilfield/project area and source project are resolved.
blocking_gaps: Primary Jha et al. (2018) record not yet extracted; API, pressure, porosity/permeability ranges, viscosity, oil saturation and target-specific label require evidence; training manifest overlap unknown.

technique_class_candidate: Hot water chemical (not same exact target)

source_summary: Martin et al. report an implemented tertiary hot-waterflood pilot in a 2.5-acre pattern, with 600 cp oil and 4,800 bbl of tertiary production; this is an actual hot-waterflood test, not a laboratory-only case.
attributes_reported: oil viscosity 600 cp; tertiary pilot; area/production reported
independent_field_counting_rule: Count Loco as one independent field only after canonical field identity, technique label and field-level records are documented.
blocking_gaps: Primary abstract does not give all eight v2 core features (depth, temperature, pressure, porosity, permeability, API, viscosity, oil saturation); not v2-trainable from abstract alone.

field_or_case: Pelican Lake E29 hot-water injection pilot
source_summary: Cenovus-designed E29 hot-water pilot began in 2011, used one horizontal producer and two horizontal hot-water injectors, and targeted an area with dead-oil viscosity 3,000–15,000 cp. A separate field overview reports broad Pelican Lake property ranges; those field-wide ranges must not be silently treated as E29-interval measurements.
attributes_reported: depth 985–1475 ft; porosity 28–32%; permeability 300–5000 mD; API 11.5–16.5; field-wide viscosity 600–80000 cp; temperature 54–63 F; initial pressure 1800–2600 kPa; saturation 60–70%
independent_field_counting_rule: At most one Pelican Lake field group; the field already appears in OGJ2014 under polymer and therefore cannot be an unseen field for a head-to-head v1 comparison.
blocking_gaps: "Target pilot is real
column12: but the property ranges are field-wide and scope-mismatched to E29; convert ranges only under a documented
column13: versioned method and verify original sources/overlap before counting for v2."

field_or_case: Kern River field post-steam water injection
technique_class_candidate: Post-steam water injection / hot-water classification unresolved
source_summary: A review reports a 10-pattern Kern River steamflood converted to water injection in September 1975 after seven years of steamflooding; post-steam water injection reused residual heat and maintained pressure. This is not automatically equivalent to a stand-alone hot-waterflood target.
attributes_reported: post-steam water injection; reported 22% OIP contribution
independent_field_counting_rule: Kern River is one field group and already occurs as steam in OGJ2014; it cannot be used as an unseen field.
blocking_gaps: Clarify taxonomy for a post-steam stage; source-compatible v2 core features and project-level rather than field-wide values not assembled.
